cheribsd-revocation.oracle: PREDICTED, not measured. CheriBSD's revocation sweeps capabilities to freed heap memory, so the stale pointer SHOULD be revoked and the probe fault -- but only if the sweep has run between the free and the access. The reduction frees and re-allocates immediately, the case least favourable to revocation, so a clean reading here would be about sweep TIMING rather than about the defect.

title: a flush flag was written into a watcher the poll it had just called may have freed
object: a log watcher, one calloc(1, sizeof(logger_watcher))
lifetime_ender: free(w) inside logger_thread_close_watcher, reached from logger_thread_poll_watchers
shape: a helper that may free the object its caller is standing on
allocator_layer: the platform allocator itself: one direct malloc/calloc/getline allocation, with neither memcached suballocator in the path.
fidelity: model consumer, real lifetime: the allocation, the free and the later access through the stale pointer are upstream's, quoted in PROVENANCE.md. The later access is `w->failed_flush = true;`, a WRITE into the freed watcher.
status: built 2026-10-08; native arms measured by runners/run-native.sh in the same commit. The platform arms are declared predictions.
live_proof: absent at the pin: this fix was SUPERSEDED by 3bc58f6ea55a rather than reverted, so `grep -c 'if (watchers[x] != NULL) {'` on 1.6.45:logger.c is 0 while the successor's `if (watchers[x] == NULL) {` appears twice. The unguarded write is at e7793811f8c8^ and is absent from the pin. A fix-reversal.
nested_why: the object came straight from malloc / calloc / getline, with neither slabs.c nor cache.c between it and the request. So under this inventory's axis, WHO ALLOCATED THE OBJECT, this row is NOT nested. Its sibling ../allocator-repros holds the nested ones.
distinguishing: the free is two calls deep and CONDITIONAL on the peer having gone away, so nothing at the write's own line suggests the object might be gone -- the fix's own comment is the documentation: 'Oddity; poll_watchers can free *w, recheck it.' The close also nulls the global slot `watchers[w->id]` but cannot null the caller's local `w`, which is what leaves the dangling pointer.
